decks.title: Blunder-proof: answer the threat
decks.blurb: The opponent has just made a threat. Spot it and play the right defence automatically. These are the most common ways games are thrown away.

cards.title: Queen and bishop on f7
cards.text: White's queen and bishop both aim at f7. Defend, and if you can, gain time doing it.
cards.why: **3...g6** defends f7 indirectly by kicking the queen (4.Qf3 Nf6 is fine for Black), and **3...Qe7** defends f7 directly. The natural 3...Nf6?? allows 4.Qxf7#.

wrong.Nf6: Qxf7# — checkmate! f7 was attacked twice and defended only by the king.

cards.title: Knight and bishop on f7
cards.setup: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5
cards.text: White attacks f7 twice. What is the principled answer?
cards.why: **4...d5!** blocks the bishop's diagonal. After 5.exd5 Black plays 5...Na5! rather than 5...Nxd5?, which allows the Fried Liver (6.Nxf7) or the Lolli (6.d4).

wrong.d6: Too slow: 5.Nxf7 wins material (fork of queen and rook).

cards.title: Don't take the queen!
cards.setup: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Bg4 Nc3 g6 Nxe5
cards.text: White's knight just ignored the pin and took on e5. The queen is hanging on d1. What do you do?
cards.why: **5...dxe5** and Black is only a pawn down after 6.Qxg4. Taking the queen loses to Légal's Mate: 5...Bxd1?? 6.Bxf7+ Ke7 7.Nd5#.

wrong.Bxd1: 6.Bxf7+ Ke7 7.Nd5# — Légal's Mate! A free queen is often a trap: check what the opponent's other pieces can do.

cards.title: Battery on the e-file
cards.text: Black's queen and rook are lined up on the e-file. What is Black threatening, and how do you stop it?
cards.why: Black threatens **...Qe1+! Rxe1 Rxe1#**, a back-rank mate. Making *luft* (h3, g3) or guarding e1 again stops it. Make it a habit: when the back rank is weak, make luft before it's too late.

wrong.Qxh7+: After Kxh7, ...Qe1+ is still coming. Don't panic — defend the back rank.
wrong.b3: This ignores the threat: ...Qe1+! Rxe1 Rxe1#.
wrong.Kf1: The king walks toward the e-file battery and stays exposed. Simply make luft with h3 or g3.

cards.title: Battery against h7
cards.text: White's queen on d3 and bishop on b1 form a battery against h7. Find a sound defence.
cards.why: White threatens **Qxh7#**. **...Nf6** covers h7 with a piece (the most natural defence), while ...f5 or ...g6 blocks the diagonal at the cost of a slight weakening. ...h6? does nothing: Qh7# is still mate.

wrong.h6: Qh7# is still mate. Defend h7 or block the diagonal.
wrong.Re8: Qxh7+ Kf8 Qh8# — the f8-square was the king's only escape.

cards.title: Morphy's queen and bishop
cards.setup: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Bg4 dxe5 Bxf3 Qxf3 dxe5 Bc4
cards.text: This is the Opera Game position (Morphy, 1858). White threatens something on f7. Defend it.
cards.why: White threatens **Qxf7#**. In the Opera Game Black played **6...Nf6** 7.Qb3!, and Morphy's double attack on f7 and b7 kept the initiative. Every defence must cover f7 or block the diagonal.

wrong.Nc6: Qxf7# — mate! Always ask what the opponent's last move threatens.
wrong.Bc5: Qxf7#. The bishop develops, but f7 is still attacked twice and defended once.

decks.title: Opening traps & tactical patterns
decks.blurb: Classic traps and mating patterns. Play them from both sides until they're automatic.

cards.title: Englund Gambit Trap
cards.setup: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Bc3
cards.text: White's bishop is trying to trap your queen on b2. Finish the job with mate.
cards.why: **6...Bb4!** pins the c3-bishop, and after 7.Qd2? Bxc3 8.Qxc3 **Qc1#**: the queen on c3 can't get back to c1 because her own c2-pawn blocks the way, and the king has no escape square.

cards.title: Punish the b2-grab
cards.setup: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2
cards.text: Black's queen has grabbed the b2-pawn, leaving d5 unprotected. Find the move that regains material and threatens a fork.
cards.why: **5.Nxd5!** wins the pawn back with tempo. It threatens **Nc7+**, forking king and rook, and Rb1 will chase the queen around the queenside. Grabbing a wing pawn with the queen while undeveloped, and leaving your centre loose, is a classic way to get punished. (5.Nb5 is the famous gambit try with the same Nc7+ idea, but Nxd5 is cleaner.)

wrong.Rb1: Chasing the queen first lets Black defend d5. Take the pawn with tempo while it's loose.

cards.title: Philidor's Legacy
cards.text: Queen and knight against a cornered king. Find the classic smothered mate.
cards.why: **Nf7+ Kg8 Nh6+** (double check: knight and queen) **Kh8 Qg8+!! Rxg8 Nf7#**. The king is smothered by its own pieces. The pattern was described by Lucena (1497) and later popularised as 'Philidor's Legacy'.
